title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 21 (Effect of mistakes as to law)

content.overview: Section 21 provides that a contract is not voidable because it was caused by a mistake as to any law in force in India; but a mistake as to a law not in force in India has the same effect as a mistake of fact.
content.glance: Mistake as to Indian law does not make the contract voidable; mistake as to foreign law = mistake of fact.
content.study: A contract is not voidable merely because it was caused by a mistake as to any law in force in India. A mistake as to a law not in force in India has the same effect as a mistake of fact (and may engage s. 20 if bilateral and essential). Current-law framing: classify the mistake as Indian law or foreign law; apply the corresponding rule.

sections.heading: Mistake as to Indian law
sections.body: Contract not voidable because caused by a mistake as to any law in force in India.

sections.heading: Mistake as to foreign law
sections.body: Mistake as to a law not in force in India has the same effect as a mistake of fact.

provisions.title: Effect of mistakes as to law

examples.title: Mistake of Indian statute
examples.body: Parties contract under a wrong view of an Indian statute. The contract is not voidable on that ground alone under s. 21.

hypotheticals.question: Does every legal mistake void the agreement?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Mistake as to Indian law does not make the contract voidable; only mistake as to foreign law is treated as mistake of fact.

misconceptions.trap: Ignorantia juris always voids the contract.
misconceptions.correction: Section 21: mistake as to Indian law does not make the contract voidable.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 21 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Classify as Indian or foreign law. II. Apply the corresponding rule. III. If foreign law and bilateral essential fact, link to s. 20. IV. Conclude.

examTips: Contrast Indian law vs foreign law.
